classified_samples.observation: The final RTL is the ordinary positive-edge 8-bit DFF requested. One first-time mismatch alone does not prove a prompt-defined correction; do not add an unstated initial value.
The final Boolean expression misses explicit K-map care cells. Already belongs to the separate table-validation problem, whose native failure-propagation controls remain unqualified.
Final RTL implements the stated XOR feedback DFF without reset. One first-time mismatch is insufficient evidence to invent initialization.
Final expression disagrees with explicit care cells. Keep separate from an FSM prompt factor.

The embedded interface declares a scalar output while the prose calls the object an 8-bit mux to fix. Generated RTL widens the output. Retain failure; do not infer a benchmark-specific interface answer.

The six vectors are concatenated with trailing low bits, then split in increasing output-name order from the low end. Output-name to bit-order convention is not explicitly written as one aggregate assignment; related to the independent bit-mapping factor.

Final RTL captures old sampled 1 to current 0, accumulates output, and synchronously resets the output. Reset treatment of the previous-input history is not specified sufficiently to identify the 28 mismatch causes without additional prompt-defined calibration.

Prompt explicitly assumes all three DFFs start at zero; RTL provides no initial value. Existing skill already allows explicitly required FPGA initial values, so this is separate from a new FSM edge contract.

Final dual-edge construction uses positive-edge storage on the inverted clock and a clock-selected output mux. Native mismatches alone do not isolate edge scheduling or initialization cause under the original harness.
Documented mask indices differ from the actual constant set bits. Current separate bit-mapping pilot includes this task.
Final gate disagrees with an explicitly shown input/output waveform row. Treat as waveform-to-Boolean extraction, separate from FSM timing.
The documented right shift is implemented with increasing destination index from the lower source index. Current separate bit-mapping pilot includes this task.
Prompt requires Moore output; final output directly depends on live input in both states. State memory does not encode the required sampled output distinction.

The final comments associate physical mux indices with Gray K-map column order instead of the numeric selector encoding. Related to selector-to-index mapping; avoid duplicating the current bit factor.
The concatenated mux shift calculation does not span the stated selector range correctly. Current separate bit-mapping pilot includes this task.
The final expression includes an input whose explicit waveform row must leave output low; there is a direct row contradiction.
Final Boolean expression disagrees with multiple explicitly supplied waveform rows.
Final RTL implements the stated load-select DFF submodule. One first-time mismatch is not evidence for adding an unstated initial value.
Moore output is separately registered from the old current state on the same edge as the state update, adding one unintended cycle.
Generated minterm coordinates disagree with the explicitly labeled K-map axes. Remains separate from FSM semantic guidance.
Prompt declares a four-bit vector but table labels include a fifth index. Do not silently hardcode a benchmark-specific renumbering.
Prompt waveform explicitly shows a bounded counter wrap; generated three-bit increment wraps by width alone and misses the displayed boundary. Input/clock coincidence remains a separate uncertainty.
Implemented neighbour vectors reverse the source-index direction stated in the prompt. Current separate bit-mapping pilot includes this task.
The expression disagrees with explicit care cells under the written K-map labels; do not revive unqualified table controls by changing the acceptance rule.
The final nested condition maps several distinct explicitly supplied selector values to one result; waveform lookup entries are not all represented.
Three sampling states are followed by an output-only state that neither samples the next input nor overlaps the next window, creating a dropped input every four state cycles.
Prompt asks for next-state logic but its last sentence equates the output to the current-state bit. Final RTL chooses the latter. Retain as ambiguous, not a clean causal target.

Final done storage has both combinational and clocked procedural writers. Native compile-level acceptance does not establish legal single ownership; do not duplicate the existing writer guidance factor.

The two detector states accept two consecutive asserted inputs instead of tracking the required three-sample sequence. Separately, the release pulse is registered from the old state and starts a cycle late.

BCD increments use unsized arithmetic inside concatenations, and the AM/PM toggle is tied to the hour wrap rather than the stated noon/midnight transition. Original RTL may compile after mechanical normalization; do not conflate compilation with arithmetic semantics.
The final walking outputs include falling states, and a simultaneous-bump branch is shadowed by earlier single-bump branches. The reset and fall priority themselves are implemented.
Datapath actions dispatch on next_state at the entry edge, so start detection consumes a data-count slot and the stop test is reached before all eight data samples have been consumed.

The final output algebra collapses to the current memory bit, contradicting explicit rows where output differs from observable state. Original completed response used 7,785 tokens; do not reduce the existing 8,192 cap because of this failure.

Direction is recomputed against a register overwritten every edge, so the last sensor-change history disappears after one unchanged cycle. Reset does not force all four required outputs because outputs use live sensors and a transient direction comparison.
All requested output ports are assigned, but two requested next-state equations omit their explicitly listed incoming self-loops. Current-state Moore outputs are already decoded correctly.
In the left-walking state, an outer condition prevents the left-only bump transition from being considered. Output decoding, fall priority, and dig priority are already implemented.

Prompt requires asynchronous active-high reset; actual sequential block only triggers at a positive clock edge. History recovery priority and old-PHT read order are already represented; PHT reset value is not specified in prompt and must not be inferred from the oracle.
An output-only state unconditionally returns to idle and ignores the input on the done cycle, losing a back-to-back message start shown in the supplied example waveform.

Either single bump switches either walking direction, even when that bump is not the obstacle in the current walking direction. Fall counter is already saturating, so a generic saturation hint does not explain the observed walking-only mismatches.

highest_priority_new_factor.name: pre_generation_clock_edge_and_state_contract_appendix
highest_priority_new_factor.purpose: Turn the existing generic逐拍一致 requirement into an operational internal edge/state ledger before RTL generation.
highest_priority_new_factor.proposed_generic_appendix: 时序或 FSM 题，先在内部逐边沿核对：边沿前状态和计数、该拍采样的输入、边沿后状态和数据，以及输出对应当前状态还是某次已采样事件。Moore 输出只由当前寄存状态决定，避免无意多寄存一拍；题面要求寄存事件输出时仍按规定延迟实现。连续采样窗口和背靠背消息的边界拍也要处理，不能为输出插入漏采样的空拍。每个 next-state 位要汇集全部入边，包括自环；最近一次相关事件的信息应保存到下一次相关事件。最后只输出完整 RTL。
highest_priority_new_factor.modified_factor: Only append generic task-independent text to the original rtl-generation skill. The usual repair system text also contains this skill, so both initial and repair prompts change.
excluded_changes: no task-specific answer or reference/TB-derived rule
counterexamples_and_limits: A registered event output can be required and correct; the instruction must not ban output registers globally or always replace them with combinational next-state outputs.
Task 150 already decodes its Moore outputs correctly; its observed defect is omitted self-loops, so output-only wording would miss it.
Tasks 142/152/155 share one Lemmings family but have different transition/output defects. They are a distinct follow-up guard/decode factor, not included as eight independent support tasks.
Task 135 contains conflicting current-versus-next wording and is excluded from clean support, while remaining in the failure denominator.
Tasks 034/053/104 only mismatch once at the first check under apparently prompt-faithful RTL; do not add unrequested initialization to improve the benchmark.
Task 153 already represents training precedence and old-PHT read order; its explicit asynchronous-reset omission is separate. The prompt gives no PHT initial counter value.
Task 155 already saturates the fall counter, so a saturation instruction alone cannot explain walking-only failures.
Task 147 completed with 7,785 tokens and remains a genuine denominator failure; retain 8,192 max tokens.

proposed_pilot.baseline: fresh C/P using original latest phase_full156 P common code, skills, extraction and native scoring, with only the appendix in P
proposed_pilot.qualification_proposal: Complete all samples; no measurement error, deadline, unconfirmed response or regression; all six guards remain L3 with equal calls; P total extra calls <=2; weighted mean increases; at least three targets improve across at least three distinct prompt-defined design families.

follow_up_distinct_factor.name: state_condition_and_output_table_completeness
follow_up_distinct_factor.observation: Current-state guards, simultaneous-event priority, and output decode disagree with prompt-defined transitions; all three are one related task family, not independent coverage evidence.
follow_up_distinct_factor.recommendation: Defer until the eight-task edge/state pilot has a result; do not combine factors in its first trial.
